trip.title: Vegas Road Trip — 25–29 Sep 2026
trip.description: A mobile-friendly timed car-camping itinerary from Las Vegas through Zion, Page and the Grand Canyon, 25–29 September 2026.
trip.heading: Vegas → Zion → Page → Grand Canyon
trip.introduction: Five days, two adults, one SUV — confirmed bookings, exact timing, scenic stops, campsites and a tappable route map.

bookingNotice.title: ✓ Core bookings confirmed
bookingNotice.text: Watchman Campground is booked for Friday night, and Desert View Campground is booked for Sunday night. The Tsé Bíghanílíní Upper Antelope Canyon tour is booked for Sunday 11:05–12:35; keep the 10:20 check-in target.

activities.description: Hotel breakfast.

Check out of The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas and take an Uber to Alamo at the Harry Reid airport rental center. The drive takes about 10 minutes, depending on traffic. The 08:00–09:00 UTC−7 block also includes checkout and waiting for the Uber. Arrive in time for the booked 09:00 UTC−7 pickup.

Collect the booked midsize AWD SUV, Nissan Rogue AWD or similar, at Alamo. Pickup is booked for 09:00 UTC−7 on 25 Sep. Make Ili the primary driver and pay for the rental with the United Explorer Card so the rental qualifies for the card’s auto rental collision damage waiver. Complete the paperwork, inspect the car and load your gear.

Drive to Walmart Supercenter. Google Maps forecasts 9–16 min for departure from Alamo on Fri 25 Sep at 09:30 UTC−7, checked 19 Sep. Allow about 15 min driving and 30 min to buy a cooler, ice, groceries and drinking water, then pack the cooler. Check fuel before leaving; aim to depart for Zion by 10:15 UTC−7.

Drive from Walmart on E Serene Ave via I‑215 / I‑15 / UT‑9 to Zion Canyon Visitor Center. Allow 3 hours 30 minutes elapsed; the clock advances one hour. Traffic, entrance queues or a break may add time. Use the optional Pa’rus slot for delays and check live navigation before leaving.

Go straight to the reserved Watchman campsite, check in, cook and eat a quick lunch, set up the tent and organize the essentials before the evening outing. Use nearby toilets, fill water as needed and check current Zion trail/tunnel information. Keep the setup efficient so camp is ready before sunset.

Optional only if lunch and camp setup finish comfortably early. Take a short out-and-back from the Visitor Center/Watchman area, but protect the Canyon Overlook sunset plan and be back at the SUV for the 15:55 UTC−6 departure.

photo.caption: Pa’rus Trail

activities.description: Drive UT‑9 from Watchman through the Zion–Mount Carmel Tunnel to Canyon Overlook; includes parking search. Leave by 15:55 so there is plenty of time to hike up and settle at the overlook before sunset.

Hike to Canyon Overlook, approximately 1.6 km return, then relax at the viewpoint and stay for sunset around 19:25 UTC−6. Start back immediately after sunset and use headlamps for the descent as needed.

photo.alt: View from Canyon Overlook in Zion
photo.caption: Canyon Overlook

activities.description: Drive back through the Zion–Mount Carmel Tunnel to the already-set-up Watchman campsite, allowing for tunnel traffic. This keeps a useful buffer before the announced 21:00 tunnel closure.
Return to the already-set-up campsite, cook/eat a simple dinner if needed, clean up and prep Saturday’s hiking gear and breakfast. Aim to sleep soon after 21:00 for the early Scout Lookout morning.

notes.title: If behind
notes.text: Pa’rus is optional: drop it first if timing is at all tight. Prioritize checking in at Watchman, cooking lunch and setting up the tent before leaving for Canyon Overlook. If Canyon Overlook parking fails, do not circle excessively—take a short scenic stop and return to camp. Allow another 30–60 minutes if rental pickup or shopping is slow. If pursuing Angels Landing, submit Saturday’s day-before lottery by 15:00 Utah / 14:00 Vegas time on Friday; results arrive after 16:00 Utah time. Scout Lookout itself needs no permit, but the chains section does. The announced tunnel closure is 21:00–06:00 on Sep 21–25 and 28–30; the plan targets the return tunnel crossing well before 21:00. Recheck conditions before travel.

days.title: Saturday 26 Sep
days.route: Watchman → Scout Lookout → Kanab → Horseshoe Bend → Lone Rock Beach
days.clockGuidance: Utah UTC−6 through Zion · then intentionally use Arizona UTC−7, even at Lone Rock

activities.description: Cook breakfast, fill bottles, break camp and pack the car.

Drive to Visitor Center parking and queue for the first shuttle at 07:00 UTC−6.

Buses run about every 5–10 min to The Grotto, stop 6. Estimate 25–30 min on the bus, plus queue time. Aim to start hiking by 07:45 UTC−6; includes buffer for a later bus.
West Rim hike with photos and snack rests; turn around at Scout Lookout.

photo.alt: Scout Lookout above Zion Canyon
photo.caption: Scout Lookout

activities.description:
Around 11:45 UTC−6, take a down-canyon shuttle from The Grotto to the Visitor Center.

Buses run about every 5–10 min, with no fixed departure times. Estimate 25–30 min on the bus, plus waiting time. Use the toilets and retrieve the SUV for a 12:30 UTC−6 departure. A 5–10-minute service interval does not cap the queue. If departure slips by 15–30 minutes, shorten Horseshoe Bend time to protect daylight camp setup.
Drive via UT‑9 and Mt Carmel Junction.
Quick lunch; leave by 14:15 Utah time.

Drive via US‑89 to Horseshoe Bend. Allow 1 hour 45 minutes elapsed including parking. Gain one hour on the clock in Arizona. Check navigation before departure; shorten viewpoint time if delayed to protect the 16:20 departure for Lone Rock.

Walk the 2.4 km round trip to the overlook and take afternoon photos. Allow time for water and rest after the morning Zion hike; bring water and sun protection. Return to the car by about 16:20, then head straight to Lone Rock for camp setup and sunset.

photo.alt: Horseshoe Bend near sunset
photo.caption: Horseshoe Bend

activities.description: Drive directly to Lone Rock Beach. Allow about 30 minutes; check navigation before departure. Keep using Arizona time even after crossing into Utah.

photo.alt: Lone Rock rising above Lake Powell beside Lone Rock Beach
photo.caption: Lone Rock Beach · NPS

activities.description: Enter and pay if needed, choose a conservative, accessible firm spot and set up the SUV in daylight. Follow rental-road restrictions and avoid deep or soft sand.

Relax at camp and watch sunset around 18:16 Arizona time. Cook dinner and clean up, then prep Sunday’s packed lunch, water and hiking gear. Set alarms for a 06:00 wake-up and 07:00 departure on Arizona time. Utah clocks here read one hour later.
activities.solarNote: 🌅 Sunset ≈18:16 UTC−7 Arizona time · 19:16 UTC−6 local Utah time

notes.title: Pacing
notes.text: After lunch in Kanab, head straight to Horseshoe Bend, then Lone Rock for daylight camp setup and sunset. Buy the main groceries, water and ice on Friday and check supplies and fuel before leaving Kanab; there is no planned Walmart stop this weekend. Prioritize a firm, obvious camping position over driving farther toward the water. If Zion runs late or an Angels Landing permit is obtained, rework the afternoon and shorten Horseshoe Bend as needed to protect daylight camp setup. Zion’s main-canyon shuttle starts at 07:00 for this date range and does not serve Canyon Overlook.

photo.caption: Lone Rock Beach · evening at camp

days.title: Sunday 27 Sep
days.route: Lone Rock → Wahweap → Dam Overlook → Amphitheater → Upper Antelope → Desert View → Navajo Point → Desert View Campground

activities.description: Wake, breakfast, fill bottles and break camp. Keep clocks on Arizona time; local Utah clocks read one hour later.
Allow 30 minutes to leave the beach, drive to the signed Wahweap Overlook off US‑89 and park. Keep clocks on Arizona time. If early, spend the extra time at the overlook; leave there by 07:45.
Lake Powell views and photos.

photo.alt: View over Lake Powell from Wahweap
photo.caption: Wahweap Overlook

activities.description: Drive across the dam and park.
Short walk and views.

photo.alt: Glen Canyon Dam and Lake Powell
photo.caption: Glen Canyon Dam

activities.description: Drive to the Page Shores Amphitheater access beside Big Lake Trading Post / Shell at 1501 Coppermine Road. Use permitted parking and follow signs; the sandstone area is reached on foot.

Short sandstone exploration and photos behind Big Lake Trading Post / Shell. The map pin marks the attraction; use the nearby signed access and permitted parking, then walk. Return to the car by 09:20.

photo.alt: Sandstone alcove near Page
photo.caption: Page sandstone

activities.description: Snack and schedule buffer before leaving for the tour meeting point. No Walmart stop; leave by 09:30.

Leave the amphitheater access parking by 09:30. The nearby tour meeting point is on Hwy 98 at milepost 299.8. This 40-minute block includes the short drive, parking and a generous booking buffer; target arrival by 10:10 for the 10:20 check-in.
Early-arrival buffer, 10:20 check-in, toilets and wait for the booked departure. Check-in closes at 10:35.
The booked 90-minute tour includes the operator’s shuttle rides to and from the canyon. Return to the meeting-point vehicle around 12:35.

photo.alt: Light beams in Upper Antelope Canyon
photo.caption: Upper Antelope Canyon

activities.location: Tsé meeting point → Page · quick lunch
activities.description: After the tour, drive into Page for a quick lunch and toilets. Keep it fast and leave Page by 13:15 for the Grand Canyon.

Drive from Page via US‑89 through Cameron, then AZ‑64 to Desert View. Allow 2 hours 45 minutes including a short break and east-entrance margin. Recheck live navigation; shorten the viewpoints if delayed.
Exterior viewpoints and photos. Enter the tower only if access is immediate and you can leave by 16:25.

photo.alt: Desert View Watchtower at the Grand Canyon
photo.caption: Desert View

activities.description: Buy dinner or any missing groceries before heading to Navajo Point. The deli is currently listed to close at 17:00 and the market later; recheck hours shortly before the trip. If you prefer, skip this stop and cook dinner at the campsite.
Drive west to Navajo Point and park. This is the replacement for closed Lipan Point.
Enjoy views of the Colorado River, canyon and Desert View Watchtower. Leave by 17:15 so there is plenty of daylight to settle into the booked campground.

photo.alt: Colorado River and canyon views from Navajo Point
photo.caption: Navajo Point · NPS / T. Karlovetz

activities.description: Drive back east to the booked Desert View Campground and check in at the reserved site.

Set up at the booked campsite in daylight. Cook dinner at camp or eat the food picked up from the nearby Desert View Market, then clean up and prepare Monday’s food, water and hiking gear. Sleep around 20:30–20:45.

notes.title: Protect the booking
notes.text: Leave Lone Rock by 07:00 Arizona time. Protect the 09:30 departure from the amphitheater, 10:20 tour check-in and 11:05 tour departure; shorten overlooks or skip the amphitheater if delayed. After the tour, eat a quick lunch in Page and leave town by 13:15. Allow 2 hours 45 minutes from Page to Desert View. Lipan Point and its access road are closed during the trip, so visit Navajo Point instead. If the afternoon runs late, shorten or skip Navajo first, then shorten Desert View. Yavapai Point and the Geology Museum move to Monday afternoon. Desert View Campground is booked for Sunday night; pick up dinner at the nearby market before its deli closes or cook at camp. There is no Sunday Walmart stop.

photo.alt: Upper Antelope Canyon sandstone and light beams
photo.caption: Upper Antelope Canyon · booked

days.title: Monday 28 Sep
days.route: Desert View Campground → South Kaibab → Mather Point → Yavapai Geology Museum → Hermit Road sunset → Long Jim Loop

activities.description: No-cook breakfast, break camp and final gear check. Pack for the full day; there is no midday return.
Drive west along Desert View Drive to the Visitor Center and park.

Toilets and gear check, then aim to board the eastbound Orange shuttle around 07:40 UTC−7 for South Kaibab Trailhead.

Buses run every 20 min from 06:00 to 09:00 UTC−7. Allow 10–15 min for the ride; aim to start hiking by 07:55 UTC−7.

Hike to Ooh Aah Point and Cedar Ridge, then return. Cedar Ridge is about 4.8 km return with roughly 340 m of ascent; use Ooh Aah as the shorter turnaround if heat or pace warrants, and allow more time uphill. Current access is reported open through Tip-Off with closure below it. Carry all required water—the trail has none and the trailhead filling station is currently reported off—and recheck conditions and water status before travel.

photo.alt: South Kaibab Trail descending into the Grand Canyon
photo.caption: South Kaibab

activities.description:
Around 11:25 UTC−7, take the Orange shuttle from South Kaibab Trailhead back to the Visitor Center.

Buses run every 15 min after 09:00 UTC−7, returning via Yaki Point and Pipe Creek Vista. Estimate 20–25 min riding back, plus waiting time. This block includes a small queue buffer.

Recovery snack and toilets, then walk about five minutes from the Visitor Center plaza to Mather Point. Eat lunch and rest, and buy a portable dinner inside the park before continuing. The westbound Orange shuttle is an alternative to walking, with a short ride plus waiting time.

photo.alt: Clouds and fog drifting through the Grand Canyon below Mather Point
photo.caption: Mather Point · NPS / Michael Quinn

activities.description: Continue about 0.7 mi / 1.1 km along the Rim Trail from Mather Point, or use the Orange shuttle. Visit Yavapai Point and the Geology Museum, then return to the Visitor Center by shuttle in time to leave for Hopi Point. The museum is currently listed as open daily 08:00–19:00; recheck before the trip.

photo.alt: Visitors watch sunset over the Grand Canyon from Yavapai Point
photo.caption: Yavapai Point · NPS / Michael Quinn

activities.description:
Around 14:30 UTC−7, take the Blue Route to Hermit Road Transfer, then the westbound Red Route to Hopi Point.

NPS transit data estimates about 19 min riding the Blue Route and 10 min on the Red Route, roughly 30 min on buses before waits and the transfer. Both routes run every 12 min at this time; transfer queues can take two or three buses.

Aim to reach Hopi Point by 15:45 UTC−7. Arrival by 16:00 UTC−7 is still workable if queues are long; use some of the following viewpoint time.
Enjoy Hopi Point, then walk about 0.8 mi / 1.3 km along the Rim Trail to Mohave Point with photo stops.

photo.alt: Grand Canyon view from Hopi Point
photo.caption: Hopi Point

activities.description: Relax, eat the store-bought dinner sandwich and stay through sunset.

photo.alt: Sunset from Mohave Point
photo.caption: Mohave Point

activities.description:
Around 18:25 UTC−7, board an eastbound Red shuttle at Mohave Point to Hermit Road Transfer, then transfer to the Blue Route for the Visitor Center.

Plan on roughly 10–15 min riding the Red Route, up to about 12 min waiting for each bus, and around 20 min on the Blue Route. A normal connection should take about 35–50 min total; this 60-minute block keeps a modest buffer for post-sunset queues.

Red buses run every 12 minutes until sunset, with a final return sweep about one hour after sunset. Blue buses run every 12 minutes until 19:00, then every 15 minutes until 21:00. Aim to reach the Visitor Center by 19:25; do not rely on the final Red bus.
Drive back to the saved camp area in the dark and use an available nearby pullout.
Reset the SUV, wash up and sleep.

notes.title: Full-day carry
notes.text: Take water, layers, headlamps and charging needs for the full day. After buying lunch and a portable dinner inside the park, carry dinner through sunset. The exact Long Jim pullout is not held while the SUV is away; finding an available pullout may delay setup. Orange starts at 06:00 and runs about every 20 minutes until 09:00. Allow 10–15 minutes from the Visitor Center to South Kaibab. Use the midday block for Mather Point, Yavapai Point and the Geology Museum, returning to the Visitor Center by 14:30. Red starts at 08:00; eastbound return normally stops at Mohave, Pima, Powell and Hermits Rest, with a final sweep about one hour after sunset—recheck and do not rely on the final bus. Keep the Hermit Road scope to Hopi → walk to Mohave → sunset; do not add The Abyss or Monument Creek Vista unless well ahead and willing to shorten Hopi/Mohave. If the 08:00 Orange shuttle is caught instead of 07:40, absorb the delay inside the late-morning buffer rather than cutting sunset. Budget the sunset return until 19:25, the camp drive until 19:55 and reset/sleep until 20:25. If hot weather is forecast, return to the earlier 05:30 wake-up and 06:55 hike start to reduce heat exposure on the climb back.

photo.alt: South Kaibab Trail at Grand Canyon
photo.caption: South Kaibab · morning hike

days.title: Tuesday 29 Sep
days.route: Long Jim Loop → Las Vegas → flight

activities.description: Cook breakfast, prepare the road lunch, pack and leave the campsite clean.

activities.location: Long Jim Loop → Las Vegas / Alamo area
activities.description: Drive via Williams, I‑40, US‑93 / I‑11 and I‑215 toward Alamo at 7135 Gillespie St. Budget about 5 hours of driving plus a 15-minute break. Navigate to the rental center with a chosen fuel stop rather than the generic Las Vegas city pin; use the following buffer for delays.

Packed lunch, traffic buffer, refuel and clear the SUV, then return it to Alamo at 7135 Gillespie St. Complete handover by 14:00–14:15 UTC−7. The booked return remains 16:00. Use this buffer to protect terminal arrival by 15:00.

Take the rental shuttle to your departure terminal. Allow 45–60 minutes after handover for walking, waiting, loading and the ride; finishing the return at 14:00 gives the full hour. Airport connector tunnel lane reductions are scheduled through December 2026. Target terminal arrival by 15:00.

Be at the departure terminal by 15:00 UTC−7 for check-in, security and the gate buffer before the 18:00 flight. Confirm the terminal, airline bag cutoff and any additional international check-in requirements.

notes.title: If delayed
notes.text: Remove sightseeing and discretionary breaks first. Keep fuel, car return and airport buffer. There is no Hoover Dam detour in the base plan. Keep the 07:30 camp departure and use the Vegas buffer to finish Alamo handover by 14:00–14:15 and reach the terminal by 15:00. Check live traffic before leaving; depart earlier if the forecast or airline requirements call for it.
